intermittent

/in-ter-MIT-uhnt/ - the stress falls on MIT · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Intermittent means starting and stopping at irregular intervals — active for a while, quiet for a while, never continuous.

The cabin's intermittent water pressure taught us to rinse fast: the tap ran strong for a minute, sputtered, and quit until the pump caught up.

Example

Halfway across the bridge the drizzle thickened, and Dad reached for the wiper stalk without looking. "Not full speed," he said, clicking it down a notch. "Intermittent — the rain isn't steady, so the blades shouldn't be either." The wipers swept once, rested a beat, and swept again, keeping easy time with a rain that came and went.

The setting is named for exactly what it does: the blades work in a stop-start pattern, active and then idle at intervals, instead of running continuously. Anything intermittent behaves that way — it keeps quitting and keeps returning, and the gaps are part of the pattern rather than the end of it.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

periodic: Periodic means recurring at regular, predictable intervals — the quarterly report, the monthly bill. Intermittent keeps the starting and stopping but throws away the schedule: nobody can say when the next burst will come.

sporadic: Sporadic means scattered and isolated — a few cases here and there with long empty stretches between, each one a separate event. Intermittent describes one ongoing thing that keeps cutting out and resuming, not scattered one-offs.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

continuous: unbroken from start to finish

constant: never letting up at all

Where it sits · how broken-up the flow is

occasional → intermittent → fitful

occasional vs. intermittent: Occasional is weaker than intermittent: an occasional cough interrupts an afternoon a few times, while an intermittent one keeps cutting out and starting again all day, the gaps part of its pattern.

fitful vs. intermittent: Fitful goes further than intermittent: intermittent Wi-Fi drops and returns on a rough, almost countable rhythm, while a fitful connection gives only restless, broken scraps with no rhythm left at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — inter-: between

Root — mitt-: to send, let go (Latin mittere)

Suffix — -ent: in a state of; doing

Put it together: Inter- (between) + mitt- (to send, let go) + -ent = letting go between times. Latin intermittere meant to leave gaps — to let a thing drop and take it up again — and the English word still describes exactly that: activity with pauses sent between the bursts.

Use the root in a new word: emissary: When the truce collapsed, each court blamed the other side's emissary rather than its own ministers.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / technical

Intermittent is the engineer's and the doctor's word for a stop-start pattern — intermittent wipers, intermittent fever, intermittent streams — precise and unemotional. Inside this unit, keep the lanes: something transient visits once and moves on; a hiatus is one named gap in something otherwise continuous; intermittent means the gaps themselves keep coming back.
